授業目的: ・This course provides students with a fundamental understanding of why consumers think, feel, and behave the way they do, and how this understanding can be translated into more effective marketing decisions. ・Building primarily on Solomon and Russell’s Consumer Behavior (15th Edition), the course combines established theories of consumer behavior with real-world marketing practice, particularly in B2C industries such as FMCG.・The course will also explore how consumer behavior is evolving in the age of AI and AGI.
到達目標: Throughout the course, academic concepts will be connected to practical marketing challenges. By the end of the course, students should be able to apply consumer behavior frameworks to uncover meaningful consumer insights and translate them into actionable marketing strategies.
特記事項: Note: The syllabus content was updated on November 20, 2026
授業の概要・背景:
・This course explores the fundamental principles of consumer behavior and their practical applications in marketing decision making. Students will develop an understanding of how consumers perceive, learn, feel, decide, and behave, as well as how psychological, social, and cultural factors influence their choices.

・Through a combination of academic theories and real-world case studies, the course aims to bridge the gap between consumer understanding and business practice, enabling students to translate consumer knowledge into actionable insights and effective marketing strategies.
授業方法: The course will be delivered primarily in person, although some sessions may be conducted online.

第1回:
Class 1: Understanding Consumer Behavior: From Theory to Business Practice（session1-2）
We will introduce the fundamentals of consumer behavior and its role in marketing. We will explore what consumer behavior is, why understanding consumers matters for business, and how consumer behavior theories can inform marketing decisions.

Reflection assignment (students will be asked to complete a short reflections to connect a consumer behavior topic with their real-life experiences. A few students will be asked to share their reflections orally at the beginning of the next class. The consumer behavior topic will be explained by the lecturer during the class.
第3回:
Class 2: Perception & Sensory Marketing（session3-4）
We will examine how consumers perceive and make sense of products and brands through their senses. We will explore sensation, attention, interpretation, and multisensory perception, with particular emphasis on taste, texture, smell, visual cues, packaging, and product experience in FMCG.

Reflection assignment (students will be asked to complete a short reflections to connect a consumer behavior topic with their real-life experiences. A few students will be asked to share their reflections orally at the beginning of the next class. The consumer behavior topic will be explained by the lecturer during the class.
第4回: Same as above
第5回:
Class 3: Learning, Memory & Motivation（session5-6）
We will examine how consumers learn about brands, develop associations, remember experiences, and form wants and goals. We will connect learning, memory, needs, emotions, and motivation to brand building and consumer experience.

Reflection assignment (students will be asked to complete a short reflections to connect a consumer behavior topic with their real-life experiences. A few students will be asked to share their reflections orally at the beginning of the next class. The consumer behavior topic will be explained by the lecturer during the class.
第7回:
Class 4: Attitudes, Persuasion & Consumer Decision Making（session7-8）
We will examine how consumers form and change attitudes and how they make choices. We will explore persuasion, heuristics, biases, involvement, and the limits of rational decision-making. We will also examine the consumer decision-making process, from information search and evaluation to purchase and post-purchase evaluation and discuss its implications for marketing communication and choice architecture.

Reflection assignment (students will be asked to complete a short reflections to connect a consumer behavior topic with their real-life experiences. A few students will be asked to share their reflections orally at the beginning of the next class. The consumer behavior topic will be explained by the lecturer during the class.
第9回:
Class 5: Consumption, Identity & Lifestyle（session9-10）
We will explore how consumer behavior extends beyond purchase. We will examine how consumers use and experience products, how brands and consumption contribute to identity and self-expression, and how personality, values, and lifestyles shape marketplace behavior.

Reflection assignment (students will be asked to complete a short reflections to connect a consumer behavior topic with their real-life experiences. A few students will be asked to share their reflections orally at the beginning of the next class. The consumer behavior topic will be explained by the lecturer during the class.
第11回:
Class 6: Social Influence, Culture & Global Consumer Behavior（session11-12）
We will examine how other people, groups, social identities, social class, and culture influence consumption. Drawing on the diverse cultural backgrounds of the class, we will compare consumer behavior across markets and discuss the implications for global versus local marketing strategies.

Reflection assignment (students will be asked to complete a short reflections to connect a consumer behavior topic with their real-life experiences. A few students will be asked to share their reflections orally at the beginning of the next class. The consumer behavior topic will be explained by the lecturer during the class.
第13回:
Class 7: From Consumer Understanding to Marketing Action（session13-14）
In this integrative, application-focused session, students will connect consumer behavior theories with real-world marketing decisions. Using FMCG and other business cases, students will apply consumer behavior frameworks to move from consumer observation and understanding to meaningful insights, and translate these insights into positioning, innovation, communication, and actionable marketing strategies.

Reflection assignment (students will be asked to complete a holistic reflections to connect key consumer behavior topics with their real-life experiences. A few students will be asked to share their reflections orally around the end of class-7.

学生による授業評価の方法Course Evaluation by Student: Student feedback will be collected through an end-of-course evaluation survey and used to improve the course content and lecturing effectiveness.

Feedback will be provided through in-class discussions, verbal comments on student comments, and written feedback on assignments, with a focus on both theoretical understanding and practical application.
